The operation returns one stored source-selected trajectory revision and never performs hidden multi-source fusion.
Every interval, tracklet, finalization, watermark, profile, and analysis-space input is frozen by the returned snapshot or its HISTORY_INPUT_SET resource.
When no as-of revision or outcome exists, the Provider only idempotently enqueues the exact frozen request and returns PROJECTION_PENDING; construction remains worker-owned.
The v0.7.1 Provider returns only a bounded preview and does not advertise an artifactReference until a scope-aware artifact registry round trip is qualified.
Intervals are immutable as-of projections over scoped Operational Task Events.
Open database ranges are rendered only through the effective snapshot capturedAt.
Interval input event sets remain bound to their immutable revisions while the current event set advances independently at capturedAt.

Historical trajectory is motion evidence; the network is a reference model rather than complete physical truth.
OFF_NETWORK_VALID preserves plausible movement that has no trustworthy association in the current graph.
Temporal-spatial findings are task-level derived analysis, not authoritative GOWM Operational Events.
CROSS uses only T2 junction pass candidates and preserves network-local junction identity.
Ranks only locations observed in the selected historical trajectory.
Results are task-level historical correlations, not current action recommendations.

terms.definition: A persistent object in the current or historical world model.
A persistent spatial object with geometry and version semantics.
A versioned data product dataset.
A versioned layer within a dataset.
A versioned feature identity within a layer.
A GOWM operational reality task identity, not an SDAR planning task.
A revalidatable reference derived by a capability execution.
An immutable, paged set of reference identities.
A public reference to an immutable query or plan result.
An immutable revision of a task execution interval derived from operational task events.
A pinned, ordered set of operational task events used to derive an execution interval revision.
The immutable, pinned operational task event set consumed to derive one task execution interval revision.
An immutable source-local mobility tracklet version with explicit segment and gap lineage.
An immutable finalization revision describing whether a tracklet input window is provisional, sealed, or conflicted.
An immutable, gap-preserving historical trajectory revision for one subject, task interval, and selected source.
A content-addressed deterministic set of historical input resource identities and versions.
A versioned policy and method profile controlling deterministic historical reconstruction or source selection.
A structured mention or external identifier resolves to a reference candidate.
A descriptor or catalog record describes a reference.
A reference exposes versioned geometry.
An exact inside/covered-by relationship under declared boundary semantics.
An exact contains/covers relationship under declared boundary semantics.
An exact geometric intersection relationship.
A distance-bounded relation with declared unit and distance model.
A coarse cover or index candidate that requires exact verification.
A position/reference is snapped to a directed network state.
A derived route plan relates start and destination references.
A derived plan covers required road obligations.
Two temporal extents overlap.
A time interval during which entities satisfy a proximity relation.
Evidence or events correlate with an external identifier or task.
A result evaluates an external predicate against world evidence.
A validation result evaluates a reference or result.
A validation result evaluates data snapshot currentness.
A catalog query discovers matching data products.

semanticConstraints.NO_DATA: Must not imply a negative fact.
semanticConstraints.NO_FEASIBLE_RESULT: A domain result, not an infrastructure failure.
semanticConstraints.STALE: Currentness failure, not necessarily mathematical invalidity.
semanticConstraints.AMBIGUOUS: Multiple viable candidates, not a provider failure.

definitions.COMPLETED: Execution completed according to its operation contract; currentness is evaluated separately.
definitions.PARTIAL: Only part of the declared result is available; completeness is not asserted.
definitions.NO_DATA: Must not imply a negative fact.
definitions.AMBIGUOUS: Multiple viable candidates, not a provider failure.
definitions.INDETERMINATE: Available evidence cannot determine the requested domain result.
definitions.NO_FEASIBLE_RESULT: A domain result, not an infrastructure failure.
definitions.STALE: Currentness failure, not necessarily mathematical invalidity.
definitions.FAILED: Execution failed; no successful domain result is asserted.
